solution:
The correct answer is** a - Branch of renal artery, b - Glomerulus, c - Bowman's capsule, d - Branch of renal vein.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Branch of renal artery:**

 
 
• The renal artery is a large blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the kidneys.
 
• It branches into smaller and smaller vessels within the kidney, ultimately supplying blood to the functional units of the kidney, called nephrons.
 
• The branch of the renal artery that enters the nephron is crucial for delivering blood to the glomerulus, where filtration occurs.
 
 
 
• **Glomerulus:**
 
 
• The glomerulus is a network of tiny blood vessels located within Bowman's capsule.
 
• It acts as a filter, allowing small molecules like water, glucose, and waste products to pass through its porous walls.
 
• Blood cells and large proteins are too large to pass through, remaining in the bloodstream.
 
• The filtered fluid, now called filtrate, enters Bowman's capsule.
 
 
 
• **Bowman's Capsule:**
 
 
• Bowman's capsule is a cup-shaped structure that surrounds the glomerulus.
 
• It collects the filtrate that is filtered from the blood in the glomerulus.
 
• The filtrate then passes through the renal tubules for further processing and reabsorption of essential substances.
 
 
 
• **Branch of renal vein:**
 
 
• The renal vein is a large blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood and waste products away from the kidney and back to the heart.
 
• It receives blood from the capillaries that surround the renal tubules.
 
• This blood has been filtered and reabsorbed, removing waste products and retaining essential substances.
 
• The renal vein then transports this blood to the inferior vena cava.
